children: Morocco's annual inflation rate, measured by the consumer ​price index, slowed to 0.3% in August from 0.6% a month earlier, the statistics agency said on ​Tuesday.
Food prices, the main driver ​of inflation in the country, ⁠dropped 3.9% from a year ​earlier, while non-food prices increased ​2.5%, the agency said in a statement.
Transport prices rose 7.3% following a surge ​in fuel prices due ​to the conflict in the Middle East.
Core inflation, ⁠which excludes more volatile goods and government-controlled prices, rose by 0.1% year-on-year and by 0.2% ​month-on-month.

To cushion ​the ⁠impact of geopolitical tensions on the domestic market, ​the government plans to add 20 ​billion ⁠dirhams ($2.1 billion) to its 2026 budget, including increased subsidies ⁠to ​keep public transport, ​cooking gas and electricity prices stable.
